title: Party Jollof Rice
description: Nigeria's celebration rice: long-grain rice cooked right through in a fried tomato and pepper base until every grain is orange, separate and smoky at the bottom of the pot.

image.alt: Plate of orange Nigerian jollof rice surrounded by slices of fried plantain

equipment.name: Large heavy-bottomed pot with a tight lid
equipment.notes: A thin pot scorches the base

equipment.name: Foil or baking paper
equipment.notes: Seals the pot so the rice steams

ingredients.constraint: Drain well so no extra water goes into the pot

ingredients.note: If using water, add 1 extra stock cube
ingredients.constraint: Must be hot when it goes in

ingredients.note: Gives the finished rice a glossy finish

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, rubbing it between your hands. Pour off the cloudy water and repeat 3–4 times, then drain in a sieve.
steps.completionNote: The rinse water runs almost clear.

steps.instruction: Blend the tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnets and the quartered onion until completely smooth.

cues.texture: Smooth and pourable, with no visible chunks.

image.alt: Fresh tomatoes, peppers and onions broken down for a stew base

steps.instruction: Pour the blend into a pot and boil it uncovered, stirring now and then, until it has reduced by about half.

cues.visual: Thick like a sauce; a spoon dragged through leaves a trail.

steps.safetyNote: The blend spits as it thickens. Half-cover the pot and stir with a long spoon.

steps.instruction: In your large pot, heat the oil and fry the sliced onion until soft.

cues.visual: Onions soft and see-through, not brown.

steps.instruction: Add the tomato paste and fry it, stirring often, until it changes from bright red to a deeper brick red.

cues.aroma: The sharp, tinny smell is gone.

steps.safetyNote: Paste spatters in hot oil. Keep your hand back and stir with a long spoon.

steps.instruction: Stir in the reduced pepper base, curry, thyme, bay leaves and crumbled stock cubes. Fry, stirring every few minutes, until the oil rises to the top.

cues.visual: A layer of red oil gathers on the surface and at the edges.

steps.completionNote: The base looks glossy and thick, not watery.

steps.instruction: Pour in the hot stock, season with salt and bring to a boil. Taste: it should be slightly saltier than you'd like, because the rice absorbs it.
Stir in the drained rice so it sits level and is just covered by the liquid. Cover with foil, then the lid, and cook on low heat. Don't stir.

cues.visual: No liquid left at the sides; grains swollen and orange.

steps.completionNote: Grains are tender with a slight bite. If still hard, sprinkle over 4 tbsp water, re-cover and cook 5 minutes more.

steps.instruction: For the smoky party flavour, turn the heat up for a few minutes without stirring so the bottom layer toasts.

cues.aroma: Smoky and toasty. Turn off straight away if it smells acrid.

steps.instruction: Turn off the heat, add the butter and fluff the rice from the bottom up with a fork. Remove the bay leaves and serve.

notes: Use parboiled long-grain rice: it holds its shape through the long steam.
Serve with fried plantain (dodo), coleslaw or moi moi and your choice of chicken or beef.
Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of water.
